newsitem.title: GERMANY: W. German industry 1997 outlook improves - study.
newsitem.headline: W. German industry 1997 outlook improves - study.

text.p: West German manufacturers are more pessimistic than they were in January, but a new survey released by the Ifo economic institute on Sunday showed they expect better times next year.
Participants in Ifo's "Forecast 100" survey of major west German companies expected production levels to be weaker at the end of the year than forecast in the previous survey in January.
But most manufacturers now believe industrial output in 1997 will be higher than previously forecast, although the recovery in production will remain moderate in most sectors.
Industrial output is now expected to rise 0.25 percent in 1996 from a year ago, half a percentage point down from the previous forecast, but to rise steadily throughout 1997.

"There will be an average increase of more than 1.5 percent in 1997," Ifo said. "In the first quarter, the rate of growth will be less than one percent, but in the fourth quarter it will then be more than two percent higher than the same quarter in the previous year."
Most of the particpants responded to the survey in September, although it was carried out from August until the beginning of October. The results are based on 432 responses.

The west German capital goods industry expects a slight increase in production in the fourth quarter of 1996 and "somewhat slowed" development in the beginning of 1997. On average, output in the sector will rise more than two percent.
Production in the capital goods industry will continue to be export-driven, Ifo said, adding the share of exports in total production will probably rise next year.
The raw materials sector expects a rise in output of 1.25 percent next year, while the consumer goods industry sees a rise of one percent.
